subject: Intermittent large-transfer stalls after private cutover — proposed MSS clamp and SNAT mitigation
messages:
From: Mike Allen <mike.allen@clearstone.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0500
Subject: File transfers failing after private cutover

Marissa,

We cut over Clearstone's private deployment to the new VPC-on-prem tunnel yesterday evening. Since then we've seen repeated failures for large SFTP uploads (8–50MB). Clients report stalls around 64–72KB transferred, then TCP retransmits skyrocket and the transfer times out. Small files complete fine.

Attached is a pcap captured from our on-prem gateway during an attempted upload: sftp-transfer-trace.pcap. Initial look from our side shows lots of DUP/OUT-OF-ORDER and an occasional ICMP "Fragmentation needed, DF set" from an intermediate hop. We also have a handful of conntrack logs showing SYN_RECV->EST transitions followed by no further packets.

Can Redwood help triage? Our impact window is broad, but we'd like a short-term mitigation (workaround) so production jobs don't keep failing while we discuss the permanent fix.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Allen
Cloud Ops Lead, Clearstone
ops@clearstone.io

Attachments: sftp-transfer-trace.pcap (pcap, 1.6MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mike Allen <mike.allen@clearstone.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: File transfers failing after private cutover

Mike — thanks for the packet capture and the quick heads-up. Looping in Dev (network) and Laura (solutions) to triage.

Initial asks so we can scope:
- Can you confirm whether the Clearstone gateway is doing any GRE/VXLAN overlay or IPsec with DF preserved?
- Any recent firewall/Security Group changes on your side around the cutover?
- Are the failing clients all outside the Clearstone datacenter (internet -> Clearstone -> Redwood), or do they include internal-to-internal transfers?

What we'll do first: quick conntrack dump, MTU/DF checks, and look for asymmetric routing between endpoints and our egress. If we see "Fragmentation needed" ICMP from a middle hop and DF=1 on the sessions, MSS clamp on the egress NAT/gateway is usually a quick safe mitigation.

We'll prepare a minimal playbook (one-hour maintenance window) for the MSS clamp + short SNAT mapping increase to avoid ephemeral-port exhaustion if we see conntrack churn. I'll also attach an initial checklist (proposed-playbook.md) once we confirm.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

--- Forwarded attachment: sftp-transfer-trace.pcap ---

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mike Allen <mike.allen@clearstone.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: File transfers failing after private cutover

Sharing early findings after a quick look at the pcap and our edge logs.

What I see:
- Repeated triple-dup ACKs and fast retransmits around the same offset (~65KB).
- ICMP "Fragmentation needed (code 4), MTU 1428" seen from hop 10.3.98.1 toward the client IP. The original MSS on SYN appears to be 1460.
- On our egress NAT (edge-01), conntrack shows lots of TIME_WAIT-ish entries but also many entries stuck in ESTABLISHED without traffic for several seconds. Dump attached (conntrack-dump.txt).

Hypothesis: GRE overhead (or an IPsec encapsulation) reduced effective path MTU below 1500 somewhere on the path but DF is set, so larger segments cause fragmentation-needed messages. The flow then retransmits and sometimes the NAT mapping times out on the edge, creating blackholes.

Quick checks we suggest running on Clearstone side (if you can):
1) ip route get <client-ip> from the Clearstone gateway and capture DF/MSS behavior.
2) sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc (should be 0 on linux normally) — but if disabled, you'll still get ICMP when DF=1.
3) Check if intermediate VPN appliances are clamping/fragmenting and whether they preserve ICMP messages.

Short-term mitigation I can implement from our side (no kernel changes, low risk):
- Enable MSS clamping to 1400 on our egress NAT on the tunnel interfaces.
- Temporarily increase SNAT ephemeral port pool and conntrack max to reduce churn.

I'll draft the playbook and will not apply without your signoff and a short maintenance window.

Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: conntrack-dump.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mike Allen <mike.allen@clearstone.io>, Clearstone Cloud Ops <ops@clearstone.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -0500
Subject: Proposed mitigation window — MSS clamp + SNAT bump

Mike / team,

Thanks — based on the evidence Dev shared, here's a proposed low-risk plan to get your uploads stable while we pursue the permanent fix:

Planned maintenance window: Fri 20 Nov 2026 22:00–22:30 UTC (we can shift earlier if you prefer).
Actions (all reversible):
- Enable MSS clamping to 1400 on Redwood egress tunnel (edge-01, edge-02) for traffic bound to Clearstone prefixes.
- Increase SNAT ephemeral port range on edge-01 to add +10000 ports and bump conntrack hashsize to handle the temporary load.
- Monitor SFTP throughput and conntrack states for 30 minutes; roll back immediately on any unexpected failures.

Impact: brief (sub-second) TCP reset risk on active connections during the clamp change; new connections should negotiate smaller segment sizes and proceed. No config push to your gateways needed.

If you approve, Dev and I will run the change and monitor. Post-change we'll capture a follow-up pcap to verify no more ICMP fragmentation-needed and that transfers complete.

Attached is the operational playbook draft (proposed-playbook.md) and the Atlassian ticket we'll update: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/NETOPS-4321.

Please reply with APPROVE or a requested time change.

Marissa

--- Attached: proposed-playbook.md ---

From: Mike Allen <mike.allen@clearstone.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearstone Cloud Ops <ops@clearstone.io>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposed mitigation window — MSS clamp + SNAT bump

APPROVE.

Please proceed at the proposed time. Two quick questions before you run:
- What's the exact rollback command if we see regression? (We prefer one-liner revert steps.)
- Any expected latency or throughput change for ongoing small API calls? We need assurance this won't affect sub-1500 byte RPC traffic.

Thanks,
Mike

On the rollback: reply with the one-liners and we'll standby.

Mike Allen
Cloud Ops Lead, Clearstone

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Mike Allen <mike.allen@clearstone.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposed mitigation window — MSS clamp + SNAT bump (post-change notes)

Quick follow-up and recommended permanent actions after the mitigation ran:
- The MSS clamp at 1400 removed the fragmentation-needed ICMP from the path; we saw successful multi-GB test transfers complete.
- No observable impact to small RPCs; they remained sub-ms within our monitoring baseline.
- Rollback one-liner (if needed): iptables -t mangle -D POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1400 (and remove same-line on both edges).

Permanent fixes to consider (priority order):
1) Work with the intermediate VPN vendor to enable proper PMTU discovery across the tunnel (ensure ICMP is forwarded).
2) If GRE/VXLAN overhead is the cause, set MTU on the Clearstone gateway >1500 or enable jumbo MTU on path where feasible.
3) If SNAT exhaustion recurs, consider mapping long-lived clients to static SNAT pools and expanding conntrack tuning.

I'll put the post-mortem into NETOPS-4321 and schedule a 30-minute follow-up with Clearstone next week to coordinate longer-term changes.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
